public_rationale: The January 6, 2024 Marcus–Southen article identifies recognizable copyrighted material in Midjourney outputs as its subject [e2]. In his report published that day, Piltch describes his own Midjourney test producing Woody and Buzz from “animated toys,” a prompt borrowed from Marcus and Southen that names neither character [e1]. This supports replication of the central phenomenon by the claim’s January 6 cutoff [e1, e2].
limitations: The report does not establish a replication rate or success across all services; several returned generic toys [e1].
The exact dates when Piltch ran the tests are not stated.
The original article’s body was unavailable; comparison relies on its opening caption and Piltch’s description [e1, e2].
The evidence does not establish legal copyright infringement.

statement.excerpt: Lastly, Avram Piltch from Tom‘s Hardware has already replicated the gist of our results:
statement.document_title: The potential GenAI copyright infringement plot thickens

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that Piltch conducted his own tests and obtained recognizable copyrighted characters from image generators, including through prompts that did not name those characters.
Replicating the gist means reproducing the central phenomenon, without requiring identical images, success on every attempt, or confirmation of every legal and technical conclusion.
The period covers the replication already reported by the post date. No earliest date is specified.
Independent testing means Piltch generated his own results; it does not require that he had no contact with Marcus and Southen.
criteria.support_condition: A report available by the post date documents Piltch's own tests producing recognizable copyrighted characters, including from prompts that omit their names, matching the central reported phenomenon.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited report shows that Piltch merely repeated the authors' assertions without conducting tests, or that his tests failed to reproduce the central phenomenon.
